name: SIL: DEMONSTRATED GAP -- Fan Failure during PAN_DET is not interlocked
description: Fan is off for the entire PAN_DET dwell (power_set_level(5) is active) yet the state machine reaches PREHEAT normally with no fault -- proves check_safety_interlocks() is not called from state_pan_det_update() (only from state_preheat_update() and state_heating_update()). This is a defense-in-depth gap, not a hardware-interlock gap: OCP/OVP/thermal comparators (33ns/9ns/<1ms) remain independent of this software path. NOT part of the required coverage matrix (transition_table.yaml defines no PAN_DET fault row) and intentionally has no hard_assertions -- the current, unsafe behavior is what this scenario documents. Firmware fix (adding check_safety_interlocks() to state_pan_det_update()) is out of scope for this suite; see plan 031 audit note.
finding: SAFETY GAP (demonstrated, not fixed): fan failure injected throughout PAN_DET produces no fault; the machine proceeds to PREHEAT with power_set_level(5) applied and no interlock check. See state_handlers.c state_pan_det_update() vs state_preheat_update()/state_heating_update().
legacy_only_reason: The fan is off for 3 rows (300 ms at the legacy SIL's 100 ms update). PAN_DET ends after 3 updates, 30 ms at the firmware's 10 ms cadence, so on the C1 target the fan is still off when PREHEAT starts and the PREHEAT interlock (correctly) latches FAULT_FAN_FAILURE before row 3. The replacement holds the PAN_DET dwell for 1 s and runs in both modes.

name: SIL: C1 Pt100 Element-Parallel Leakage (HEATING)
description: A leak develops in parallel with the Pt100 element from tick 85 while the pan heats: over 40 s the pan, and the rim NTC under it, climb from 92 to 105 degC while the leaky Pt100's reading sags to 75 degC (-0.43 K/s, under D1's -0.8 K/s trigger), then all hold. The MAX31865 sees an ordinary in-range resistance. The rim cross-check finds the reading 30 K below the rim for 30 s, D1's probe finds contact intact (PROBE_PASSED), and the cross-check fires again with the rim not falling and the reading not rising: the second chained cycle latches FAULT_PROBE_LEAKAGE. The rim stays under the setpoint-relative rim limit for the 100 degC target (125.1 degC, D-RIMLIM), so the chain is what latches. (Before D-RIMLIM this trace held the pan at 140 degC over a 100 degC reading; that is now the rim limit's scenario, which latches first.)
c1_only_reason: A C1 runtime check (main/pan_control.c, components/control/pan_leak_check.c; DECISIONS D-LEAK) on the C1 rim cross-check and D1 probe: the legacy loop has neither.
latency_bound_note: Latency counts from the end of the perturbation (tick 484). The reading falls 25 K below the rim at tick ~418 (30 K x f >= 25 K, f = 0.83); each leak cycle is the 30 s cross-check hold plus the 18 s probe (D1's 30 s hold-off runs under the next hold), and a hold restarts whenever the command drops to 0: two cycles plus one restarted hold, 2 x 48 s + 30 s = 126 s from tick 418, is tick 1678, 1194 rows after 484; 1250 rows. Observed 901.

name: SIL: C1 Rim Above the Setpoint Envelope (HEATING)
description: DECISIONS D-RIMLIM. A leak develops in parallel with the Pt100 element from tick 85: over 10 s the pan, and the rim NTC under it, climb from 92 to 140 degC while the leaky Pt100 reads only up to 100 degC (the target). No pan held at 100 degC can make the glass hotter than 114.1 degC (the glass envelope: w 0.646-0.955 of the pan, the rest coil-eye air at up to 139.7 degC); with the rim channel's hot tolerance stack there (11.0 K: bead corner, rail, self-heating) the limit is 125.1 degC. The rim crosses it rising and stays over it, not falling, for 5 s: FAULT_PROBE_LEAKAGE, before the cross-check chain could complete.
c1_only_reason: A C1 runtime check (main/pan_control.c, components/control/pan_rim_limit.c; DECISIONS D-RIMLIM) on the C1 rim NTC and the loop's setpoint and estimate: the legacy loop has neither.
latency_bound_note: Latency counts from the end of the perturbation (tick 184). At the trace's 92 degC start the rim node sits at the driver's saturation bound (2900 mV at ATTEN3, ~92 degC), so take the rim VALID only from the leak's start (tick 85). The rule needs 31 s of VALID history (the 30 s fall window, 1 s slots) and then 5 s over the 125.1 degC limit, which the rim passes at tick ~154 plus the driver's 1 s filter: at the latest tick 85 + 310 + 50 + 10 = 455, 271 rows; 300 rows. Observed 166.

name: SIL: C1 Rim Above the Setpoint Envelope (PREHEAT)

A leak develops from tick 85 while the pan heats from 80 degC: over 10 s the pan and the rim climb to 150 degC while the leaky Pt100 reads only up to 85 degC, so the estimate stays under target - 10 K and the machine stays in PREHEAT. The rim becomes VALID above ~92 degC (tick ~102), and the limit for a 100 degC target is 125.1 degC: once 30 s of VALID rim history exist and the rim is not falling, 5 s over the limit latch FAULT_PROBE_LEAKAGE.
c1_only_reason: A C1 runtime check (main/pan_control.c, components/control/pan_rim_limit.c; DECISIONS D-RIMLIM) on the C1 rim NTC and the loop's setpoint and estimate: the legacy loop has neither.
latency_bound_note: Latency counts from the end of the perturbation (tick 184). The rim turns VALID at ~92 degC, tick ~102; the fall window needs 31 s of VALID history (tick ~412), then 5 s over the limit plus the 1 s filter: tick ~472, 288 rows; 400 rows. Observed 267.

name: SIL: C1 Cold-Soak Leak Before Heating (PREHEAT)
description: DECISIONS D-SOAK. A temperature-independent 1 kohm leak in parallel with the Pt100 from power-up (moisture, a conductive film): soaked at 35 degC the leaky element reads ~102 ohm, 5.2 degC, inside the C1 window (above the 84.27 ohm short threshold). The unit idles 40 min (>= the 30 min soak plus history), then the start press: PREHEAT entry freezes the coil-off history and the first control period, before any power, finds the heatsink NTC (35 degC, VALID) 29.8 K above the Pt100 through the 15 min window, over the 12.9 K threshold, with the rim NTC saturated: FAULT_PROBE_LEAKAGE. The leak never reaches a cook.
c1_only_reason: A C1 check (main/pan_control.c, components/control/pan_cold_soak.c; DECISIONS D-SOAK) on the heatsink NTC driver (components/sensors/hs_ntc.c, D-HSNTC) and the C1 Pt100 reading: the legacy loop has neither.
latency_bound_note: Timed from the first trace row; PREHEAT entry ran during the boilerplate (pan_control_begin froze the history), and the first control period (100 ms) evaluates the check before it commands power: at most one period plus one row, 2 rows.

name: SIL: DEMONSTRATED GAP -- Fan Failure during a 1 s PAN_DET dwell is not interlocked
description: No pan and the fan off for the first 10 rows of PAN_DET (power_set_level(5) active), then the pan is placed and the fan restarts: the machine sits in PAN_DET for 1 s with the fan off and no fault, then reaches PREHEAT normally. Same gap as the legacy scenario, at a dwell that outlasts a 100 ms row at either cadence. NOT part of the required coverage matrix and intentionally has no hard_assertions.
finding: SAFETY GAP (demonstrated, not fixed): fan failure injected throughout PAN_DET produces no fault; the machine proceeds to PREHEAT with power_set_level(5) applied and no interlock check. See state_handlers.c state_pan_det_update() vs state_preheat_update()/state_heating_update().
